newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Albright will shorten China visit -- spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Albright will shorten China visit -- spokesman.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will shorten her planned trip to Beijing by one day because of the death of paramount Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, her spokesman said on Thursday.

The spokesman, Nicholas Burns, said that instead of holding talks in the Chinese capital on Monday and Tuesday, Albright's meetings will be on Monday only and she expects to depart for Washington on Tuesday before Deng's funeral takes place.

"Obviously it's the right thing to do to leave before the funeral and to accede to all the wishes of the Chinese. We understand completely why they would want to compress the schedule," Burns told reporters.
This means what Burns called "certain ceremonial events" and perhaps a news conference with Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen will not be held because of the mourning period.
Albright, on an 11-day, nine-nation trip through Europe and Asia, had been due to visit Beijing next Monday and Tuesday. This is her first overseas trip since becoming secretary of state last month.
The funeral for Deng, who died on Wednesday at the age of 92, has been set for Tuesday. The Chinese government have asked foreign governments not to send delegations to the funeral.
